value: A relatively small gun for use on destroyers and smaller ships.
A small gun with a powered mount to allow it to track targets quickly.
A small gun with a gun shield to protect the crew from shell splinters and harsh weather.
A pair of small guns in a powered, armored mount.
A small gun in a special mount, allowing it to engage airplanes as well as surface targets.
A small gun with a high angle mount and gun shield, allowing it to engage airplanes as well as surface targets.
A small gun in a high angle enclosed turret, allowing it to engage airplanes as well as surface targets.
A small, rapid-fire gun in a high angle powered turret, allowing it to engage airplanes as well as surface targets.
A large-caliber cannon dating from before the Great War.
A set of large-caliber cannons in a heavily armored mount. A redesign of the turret allows for higher gun elevation, thus increasing the range.
A heavily armored mount for heavy guns, incorporating a number of new technologies to increase accuracy and firing speed.
The ultimate evolution of heavy firepower, this heavily armored mount allows for a high degree of accuracy over long distances.
The biggest gun ever mounted on a ship, these massive cannons were designed to penetrate any feasible armor at any distance.
A compromise between rate of fire and weight of shell, this gun is intended for the use in light cruisers to defeat smaller ships.
This gun represents a logical evolution from previous models, and is intended to allow light cruisers to have a comfortable advantage in firepower over destroyers and older cruisers.
Incorporating a number of new technologies, this lightly armored mount further increases the gap between the main batteries of destroyers and light cruisers.
Designed from the ground up for a high rate of fire, this mount was created to allow light cruisers to disable even bigger enemies through a multitude of hits.
Designed from the ground up for a high angle of fire, this mount was created to allow light cruisers to engage even bigger Ships and Aircraft.
While unable to do significant damage to battleships, this medium gun allows a heavy cruiser to confidently engage lighter ships and other cruisers.
An evolution of an earlier design, this gun was made to keep pace with the increases in armor and the longer ranges at which naval battles are fought.
While not the biggest gun one can feasibly mount on a cruiser, this cannon strikes the best balance between weight of armament and fire power and can reliably defeat cruiser-armor.
With caliber restricted by existing ammunition supplies and with an eye to retrofit older ships, this new gun features an advanced auto-loading system to drastically improve the rate of fire.
Housed in a casemate on the ship's side, this light cannon gives larger ships some measure of defense against smaller ships.
A small turreted mount for rapid-fire cannons, designed to defend capital ships against destroyers and torpedo boats.

By combining the duties of the heavy anti-air gun and the secondary battery, this mount drastically boosts the anti-air capabilities of a ship while also providing some measure of defense against smaller surface targets.
Housing dual purpose secondary guns in a turret greatly increases the crew protection.
Powered twin dual purpose turrets allow for a large increase in firepower.
Created for rapid fire against all forms of target these are the ultimate secondary weapons.
A central station high up in the ship's mast determines the range to the target and transmits that information to the gun mounts.
A central director station fires all guns simultaneously at the command of the gunnery officer.
A mechanical computer in the ship continuously updates range and bearing to target from information fed to it by rangefinders and other sensors.
A more complex mechanical computer considers a large variety of factors when calculating the ballistic solutions to engage the target.
A set of mid-sized torpedoes that can be mounted on surface warships.
By mounting another torpedo tube in the mount, a surface ship can fire a larger spread with higher chance to hit.
Larger torpedoes can carry a bigger warhead, doing significantly more damage to the target. This requires the launcher to have fewer tubes, however.
Having solved the mechanical issues of launching large torpedoes from surface ships, this advanced model can also be rapidly reloaded for another salvo.
A basic set of torpedo tubes that can be reloaded from inside the submarine.
A larger torpedo room allows more torpedo tubes to be mounted. It also provides slightly more living space for the crew.
A set of larger torpedo tubes allows submarines to launch bigger torpedoes.
The addition of an electric loading ram allows torpedo tubes to be reloaded within minutes.
A set of heavy machine guns provides a small amount of close-in defence against airplanes.
A small automatic cannon throws a significantly larger shell, killing an attacking aircraft in a few hits.

Previous calibers of guns have proven too light to reliably kill an attacking airplane before they can release their ordnance. A larger shell requires a bigger gun, but has a significantly higher chance of destroying the target when they actually hit.

The latest model of anti-air guns features a powered mount to be able to track fast-flying targets and an advanced director system to coordinate the fire of several gun positions against a single target.
Modifications for a surface ship to carry and deploy naval mines.
Gear to deploy the various sweeping equipments.
Modifications to the hull of a submarine, allowing it to deploy a number of mines.
A simple set of rails allows depth charges to be rolled off the stern of the ship when the ship drives over the submerged target.
Using a small explosive charge, this device throws a depth charge quite some distance, allowing a single ship to drop a pattern of depth charges across a larger area.
A projector for a smaller depth charge with a contact fuze, allowing the ship to engage a target without breaking sonar contact.
An evolution of the previous model, this mortar can fire a significantly larger charge over a longer distance.
A device that allows the submarine to run its main engines underwater, enabling it to recharge its batteries without exposing itself to attack by surfacing.
Improvements to the design of the schnorkel reduce the problems when using the main engines in heavy seas while reducing the probability of the schnorkel being detected on radar.
A simple airplane launcher propels a small scout plane into the air.
An improved launch mechanism that allows the ship to launch a larger plane with greater range and speed.
Equipment for refueling and recovering seaplanes, keeping them operational with less reliance on shore-based resupply.
While the earliest seaplane tenders were converted merchant ships, newer types are purpose-built and have greatly improved seaplane support capabilities.
A submarine-mounted launcher for guided and ballistic missiles.
A submarine-mounted launcher for nuclear ballistic missiles.
First iteration of the new engine types, allowing submarine to remain operational underwater for a longer time, at the cost of vastly increased fuel consumption and reduced ship range.
New version of the air-independent propulsion systems, offering better performance at the lower fuel consumption.
We have reached the pinnacle of what we think can be achieved with AIP Engines. This engine offers excellent speed, while at the same time retaining fuel consumption at acceptable levels.
Rubber tile coating that is designed to reduce the range at which ship can be detected by both passive and active sonar.
Torpedoes that carry a nuclear warhead, providing a highly effective weapon against enemy ships, at the cost of higher risk for accidents.
A large open area inside the ship that allows the servicing and arming of wheeled airplanes. Adding further hangar space to a ship dramatically drives up cost.
Open area that allows to service, refuel and resupply airplanes and prepare them for their missions. Allows to store and use non-carrier plane variants.
Open area inside the ship that allows the servicing and arming of wheeled airplanes. Much smaller and cramped than hangars on the Fleet Carriers.
A watertight compartment and catapult equipment allowing a submarine to carry, launch and recover a small number of seaplanes.
A simple set of hydrophones to track a submerged target by the sound it makes.
An active noise emitter that sends a short 'ping' into the water, then listens for the echo from a submerged submarine hull.
Improved active sonar array using stronger signal pulses and directional scanning.
State of the art sonar system, providing superior tracking of the submerged targets.
A simple radar set that operates in the 50 cm wavelength range allows the detection of surface ships even in bad weather at a range of more than 10 kilometers.
An improved radar set working in the 30cm wavelength range can accurately measure the range and bearing of even a small ship at ranges of over 25 kilometers.

Equipped with cavity magnetrons, this radar set allows not only the detection of very small targets but even detecting the splashes of shells. This allows for true blind-fire against targets, even at night or in bad weather.
Working in the centimeter wavelength range, this radar set is fully integrated into the ships gunnery control and allows highly accurate gunfire control in all weather conditions.
Extended fuel storage allows greater operational range.
A small set of steam turbines can propel a small ship at great speed or power a larger ship at slower speeds.
Using high-pressure boilers, the same weight and space of machinery can produce a higher output.
New developments in materials allow for much higher steam pressure and thus greater power output.
Improved engine layouts and turbine gearing allow higher efficiency for the same amount of weight.
A combination of diesel and electric engines allow a submarine to operate underwater at a reasonable speed.
A more powerful diesel engine gives the submarine the ability to sprint into position when it detects a target.
New materials and production methods allow for the creation of engines that can run longer at full power.
Advanced engines with turbochargers are able to run much faster for a brief period, either to chase targets or to recharge the batteries quicker.
A small reactor that provides nuclear propulsion for submarines, ensuring extended underwater endurance and efficient operation for modern naval fleets
A basic set of boilers providing steam to an ungeared turbine.
A steam turbine equipped with gearing is dramatically more efficient, allowing the extra weight to be used for additional power.
Improved boiler arrangements give higher steam pressure for more power.
Advanced materials make this engine able to run much longer at high load.
Intended to free up weight for guns and armor, this engine was never designed to give particularly high speed.
Dramatically more powerful than previous designs, this engine is intended to give a heavy ship a comfortable speed margin over older models.
As guns and armor grow in weight, this engine was designed to allow for higher speeds to chase down fleeing enemies or keep the range open against superior enemies.
Designed with new materials and improved boiler design, this powerplant is intended to allow a modern battleship to keep up with fast carriers and cruisers.
A powerful nuclear reactor, capable of powering the heaviest of ships without need for refuelling.
A basic set of engines allow a mid-sized carrier to reach the speeds necessary for the safe operation of aircraft.
This new powerplant is designed to allow a carrier to outpace most older cruisers and some destroyers, allowing it to evade enemy surface forces.
An engine designed to allow even large carriers to move at very high speeds.
This powerplant was designed to equip a modern 'fast carrier' intended to function as the centerpiece of a carrier group.
A powerful nuclear reactor, capable of powering colossal carriers without need them needing to refuel.
Designed to protect a ship against guns of its own caliber, this armor scheme ensures that every part of the ship is well-protected according to its usefulness.
Designed to protect the ship against smaller guns, this armor scheme weighs far less to allow for higher speed.
Featuring an inclined belt, this armor scheme is designed to protect a ship of the line against guns of its own caliber.
A compromise between speed and protection, this armor scheme is designed to defend a ship against the guns of cruisers and destroyers.

A radical departure from previous armor schemes, this design creates a heavily-armored citadel at the center of the ship but sacrifices protection for other parts of the ship. It is intended to defend a ship against guns of its own caliber.

Designed with an eye towards weight limitations, this armor scheme attempts to maximize protection for the vital parts of a ship by leaving other areas exposed. This scheme is not supposed to stand up to battleship-grade weaponry for long.
The last word in armor design, this armor scheme is intended to defeat all known main battery projectiles, allowing a ship so equipped to engage and sink any other battleship in the world today.
An armor scheme intended to give a cruiser a slight edge when fighting against destroyers and other lightly-armed ships.
A heavier belt intended to allow a cruiser to engage older light cruisers and smaller ships with a good deal of protection.
Copying methods used for armoring battleships, this armor scheme is designed to keep pace with developments in armaments around the world.
This armor scheme attempts to maximize protection over the areas absolutely needed to keep a ship afloat and in the fight, at the cost of all other areas.
Heavy armor plates protect the hangar spaces against hits by enemy bombers at the cost of less working space.
Additional construction reinforcements, ensuring stronger and more resilient construction, while also providing better resistance against the elements.
Steel-Reinforced Pykrete provides sturdier construction, capable of withstanding more damage, while offering better insulation.
Materials and methods used offer the best structure resilience and reducing the impact of weather on the ship operations.

A formidable deck gun of a caliber more commonly found on light cruisers.
Cruiser Submarines represent the pinnacle of heavy sub-surface raiding. What they lack in maneuverability and stealth, they certainly make up for in reach.
Small submarines designed for harbor raiding or light convoy raiding suit our naval doctrine perfectly.
